questions.q: What does nose breathing do that mouth breathing does not, according to the summary?
a: It filters and warms air and helps regulate blood pressure
It delivers more oxygen with every single breath
It removes carbon dioxide more quickly
It increases the size of the nasal passages
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the nose filters, heats and moistens air and releases chemicals that regulate heartbeat and lower blood pressure.

questions.q: What happened to Nestor after surgery temporarily blocked his nose?
a: His blood pressure rose by 13 points
His pulse slowed and he felt calmer
He developed a stronger sense of smell
He began sleeping much more deeply
questions.why: Lesson 1 reports that weeks of mouth breathing raised his blood pressure 13 points, quickened his pulse and left him feeling awful.

questions.q: Which breathing pace does the summary say science favors?
a: Roughly 5.5 seconds breathing in, then 5.5 out
A rapid cycle of two seconds in and out
Very deep breaths held for a full minute
Long exhales of 20 seconds or more
questions.why: Lesson 2 says shallow breaths of about 5.5 seconds each way are best for maintaining carbon dioxide levels.

questions.q: Why is carbon dioxide more than just a waste product?
a: It helps oxygen leave blood cells and widens vessels
It carries oxygen directly into the lungs
It signals the brain to breathe faster
It blocks the nose from filtering air
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that carbon dioxide helps oxygen separate from red blood cells and signals blood vessels to dilate.

questions.q: What are prana and ch'i in the traditions the summary describes?
a: An energy said to flow through all living things
Two types of breathing exercises for athletes
Ancient names for oxygen and carbon dioxide
Techniques for holding your breath underwater
questions.why: Lesson 3 says both cultures describe an energy concentrated in living things, maintained through practices like yoga and acupuncture.
